translate_en|mods/BloodPoolFX/42/media/l: Walking through a sufficiently wet tracked pool can contaminate the player's trail. In multiplayer the server decides when contamination begins and where footprints are placed.
Percentage chance that an eligible newly killed zombie or enabled dead player corpse creates a persistent pool record. In multiplayer this roll is made only by the server.
Writes persistence, migration, growth, native blood fallback, and synchronization diagnostics to console.txt. Leave off during normal play.
Master switch for new persistent blood pools and their bloody footprint trails. Existing native blood remains subject to the world's normal blood rules.
In-game days for ordinary age-based wetness to fall from 1.0 to 0.0. Rain can dry exposed blood much faster. Native Blood Splat Lifespan remains the hard upper limit.
Maximum alternating marks produced by a completely fresh pool. Drying pools automatically produce fewer prints according to their calculated wetness.
Travel distance required between server-authoritative bloody marks. Smaller values create tighter trails; larger values spread them farther apart.
Number of deterministic outward growth steps stored with each pool. More steps create smoother growth and more native floor-blood deposits.
Maximum distance from the pool center. The server stores the chosen radius in each persistent pool record so every client sees the same geometry.
Time-based drying will never thin a pool below this percentage of its original deterministic deposits. Rain and vanilla cleanup can still remove more.
When enabled, newly dead player corpses can create the same persistent blood pools as zombie corpses. Uses the shared corpse chance, growth, aging, rain, cleaning, and footprint rules.
Controls world-age wetness loss. When enabled, old pools gradually stop transferring blood to shoes. Visual thinning is controlled separately.
Multiplies blood deposited by the deterministic core and growth steps. 1.20 is the intended default, 1.00 is baseline, and 3.00 is the experimental maximum.
How much faster footprints wash away than dense pools. Default 3.0 means footprints require about one-third as much equivalent rain exposure.
When enabled, rain physically erodes persistent pools that are outside and exposed to weather. Indoor pools remain protected. Rain also reduces pool wetness rapidly.
Heavy Rain Hours to Wash Pool
Equivalent hours of full-strength rain required to completely wash an exposed pool. Lighter rain contributes proportionally more slowly. Default: 4 hours.
Normalized rain intensity below which washing is ignored. 0.10 allows light rain; increase this value if only stronger storms should clean blood.
When enabled, persistent bloody footprints on exposed outdoor squares can be washed away by rain.
Base number of deterministic native blood deposits in each growth step. Higher values create denser pools and more decals.
How long a new pool takes to finish growing while loaded. Interrupted growth progress is persisted and resumes after reload or restart.
When enabled, deterministic peripheral deposits disappear first as blood ages. Disable this to keep pools visually full while wetness can still decline.

When enabled, zombies that walk through a wet tracked pool can carry blood away in persistent footprints just like survivors. Uses the same footprint count, spacing, drying, cleaning, and rain-wash rules.

Single-player uses these values locally. In multiplayer, the server's Sandbox settings are authoritative for shared pools, drying, rain washing, and bloody trails; only Debug Logging remains client-local.
Master switch for newly created persistent pools and their bloody footprint trails.
In-game days until ordinary age-based wetness reaches zero. Rain can reduce wetness much faster. Visual thinning has its own toggle and configurable minimum stain.
Maximum marks from a fully wet pool. The count scales down automatically as the source pool dries.
Travel distance required between bloody marks. Smaller values create a tighter, denser trail.

Heavy Rain Hours to Wash Pool
Equivalent hours of full-strength rain needed to completely wash away an exposed pool. Lighter rain accumulates proportionally more slowly.
Rain weaker than this normalized intensity is ignored for washing. 0.10 allows light rain; higher values require stronger weather.
Persistent outdoor bloody footprints are washed away by rain independently from their source pool.
Base deterministic deposits added per growth step. Increase this when using very large radii so the pool stays dense.
How long each pool takes to finish spreading while loaded. Interrupted progress resumes from its persisted growth step.
Controls edge-to-center visual thinning separately from wetness. Disable this to keep pools visually full while world-age wetness can still decline.
